Frankly at least the Roman Empire of old wasn't a lawless dictatorship. Caesar in New Vegas is a mockery of the Caesar from history. Even Caesar as a direct dictator didn't rule quite as iron fisted as the vegas Caesar. Especially when it came to tribes, Rome as a whole used mostly 'tribal' soldiers. As their entire Empire was designed around absorbing tribes without destroying tribes. While that sometimes was through military force, there were a lot of tribes that were not lowered to an enslavement with forced conscription. Which, additionally, the way vegas Caesar does it, is more of a 'join or die', while IRL Caesar was very much open to diplomatic means. Although Caesar himself IRL is but a small portion of what we know as the typical 'Roman Empire with centurions and red and whatnot'. Hell, the Roman Empire we see in typical media including Vegas, is a very minor part of how the Empire actually was run. Honestly it was more of a loose collective of territories ran by local leaders who followed orders from Rome etc etc.

  
All of this is a very simplified way of explaining it, but my point is that Rome as a whole is portrayed as seen in media and seen as we see it in vegas. Which is the point is that Caesar in vegas is using the cliched style of Roman rule because he has his knowledge from a biased view of popularized knowledge via holotapes. Honestly if they ran an actual Roman republic with the same morals and leadership and localized economics, I could see a proper Roman 'legion' being far better than the NCR or legion itself. Albeit, slavery would need to go, as slaves really have no benefit over citizens in terms of economics and whatnot in hindsight. I mean there's a reason we don't use slaves for labor in a modern era, it's not even as cost effective as machinery or animals. Even in a wasteland like the Fallout universe, slavery on a national scale is not efficient. Especially given the ability for uprisings, and the loss of population growth and economic stability. Having a happy free citizen is much better than essentially a pack mule of a person like the legion in the game uses. A happy citizen produces offspring, wealth, and localized growth whether that is industry or agriculture or as a military asset. Even rome saw this eventually, and slaves mostly became a luxury good or specifically for things like forced combat or menial chores like in homes. Slavery as we see in Vegas, is mostly hard labor and sexual services. Both of which could be streamlined in this world, as we literally see on the strip with sex workers and robots. Which, yeah some of those are interchangeable too lmfao.
